Title: Approve Your AI Agents From Your Phone | Pushary
# Your agent froze, waiting for your yes. Pushary sends that one decision to your phone. Tap yes and it finishes the job while you are away, across every agent you run. Your code never leaves your machine. Tap Approve to try it. ## What is Pushary? Pushary is the control panel for AI agents. Every permission request lands in one place and reaches you wherever you are: your phone, Slack, the web app, and a full audit trail. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes, Windsurf, and any MCP agent. Your AI agents send permission requests to Pushary, which delivers them to your phone, Slack, the web app, and an audit trail. You hand off a task, finally stop babysitting it, and come back to find it stuck on a single question. 1. Hand off a long task. 2. The agent reaches a step it should not take alone. 1. Hand off the same task. Your agent should not wait 37 minutes for a single yes. It pauses at a step that needs your call. It buzzes when a decision is needed, not for every step. Your answer flows straight back to the agent. When the task finishes, you get a ping for that too. ## Get Pushary on your phone. Approve, deny, and watch your agents from anywhere. Your agent's question lands in Slack with Approve and Deny buttons. The flow pauses, asks you, and continues with your answer. Pushary auto-runs only the safe steps and pings you for the ones you cannot undo. If you do not answer, your rule answers for you, deny or hand back to the terminal. Every agent in one place. See which one is waiting on you, plus the full audit trail. Pick your agent and run it. I would kick off a task, switch to something else, and come back to find the agent had paused for a yes 40 minutes earlier. > I instantly related with the pain of coming back to my Claude Code and seeing "waiting for your permission" instead of "your task is completed.". * Is it safe to run an AI agent unattended? Approve your agents from your phone.

Title: Pushary : Pushary Forums | Product Hunt
# Pushary - Get push notifications when your AI agent finishes. Happy to hear thoughts and comments from you guys how you're getting notified with pushary :). This is exactly the rabbit hole I went down after the initial "task done" notification. The biggest time-sinks in order:. **Waiting for human input.** The agent needs a yes/no decision and just sits there. Worse than task completion because a blocked agent is burning context doing nothing. The agent hits a wall and you only find out 20 minutes later. For detection, the MCP server exposes three tools:. **send\_notification** sends a one-way push alert. The agent calls this when it finishes a task or hits an error. **ask\_user\_yes\_no** sends a push notification with a question. You tap yes or no on your phone. **wait\_for\_answer** blocks the agent until your answer comes back. Up to 55 seconds, retryable, your answer sticks around for 10 minutes. The key insight: the agent decides when it's blocked, not us. We don't try to detect agent states from the outside. The MCP tools give the AI a way to reach you. When Cursor's agent needs approval to delete a migration file, it calls ask\_user\_yes\_no("Delete the old migration?"). You tap "yes" from the couch. The agent gets the answer and keeps going. No context switch back to the IDE. This works across Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, Lovable, and anything that speaks MCP because MCP is the common protocol. The human-in-the-loop piece was the real unlock. "Task done" notifications save you 5-10 minutes per task. Decision notifications remove entire round-trips to the IDE. What kind of agent workflows are you running? Happy to help you wire it up. When claude asks for permissions, does pushary also notify you? @mcarmonas Of course, you just have to add this in a skill/rule file and it asks you a yes/no question like a G. You can really touch grass now and steer AI from your lock screen ;). Hey Aadil, tried it and this is exactly what I was looking for.
